text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: EVAL_GATE_ALERT (P1) for org=redwood-prod at 2026-03-15T14:02Z. Eval 'safety_and_quality:v5' tripped for model 'assistant-codegen-v2' — output-drift exceeded threshold (12%). Automatic page to oncall.

simon: ack — I'm oncall, looking now.

maria: on it. pulling eval diffs and sample prompts. any initial customer reports?

simon: telemetry shows ~2% of requests flagged by eval gate with hallucination/factualness drops. Top routes: /chat, /codegen. No host errors. Dash: https://dash.redwood.ai/alerts/4101234567

aj: noted. Pager path escalates to platform-oncall if unacked in 5m — I'll keep infra watch but looks model/quality related for now.

deploy-bot: Canary available: assistant-codegen-v1.9 is warm in prod pool and ready for traffic shift.

maria: sample set assembled (50 prompts). preliminary look: model invents table/column names, attributes claims without sources — looks like factualness attrition. sending short samples in thread.

simon: mitigation proposal: route 75% of chat/codegen traffic to v1.9 for immediate relief, hold rollout of v2. Also lock model config.

maria: running quick compare v2 vs v1.9 (50 -> 500 prompt batch). will report.

simon: command to set routing override (internal):

```
rwctl route set --selector="route:/chat" --model="assistant-codegen-v1.9" --pct=75 --reason="eval gate trip 4101234567"
```

aj: applying feature-flag route now. Confirming 75% shift.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident 78923 acknowledged by simon.

maria: quick artifacts: failing prompt example -> "Generate a migration to add a billing table"; v2 invents non-existent external service and references fake invoice schema. v1.9 returns conservative schema and notes uncertainty.

les: tagging in runtime — I see a kernel normalization change pushed at 2026-03-15T13:35 in runtime-build-107. That change could affect attention weights and lead to generation drift. I'll investigate.

aj: infra shows no host-level regressions; memory/latency OK.

simon: action checklist: (1) route 75% to v1.9 (done), (2) pause v2 rollout, (3) run full batch eval (10k prompts) to measure scope, (4) consider kernel rollback if correlated. Escalate to SEV1 if customer impact increases.

maria: starting batch eval now; ETA ~7m. collecting logs and attribution traces.

les: preparing kernel rollback plan to runtime-build-106 (pre-change). ETA ~10m, will do a rolling update, no host restarts expected.

deploy-bot: Initiating rollback: runtime -> runtime-build-106 (rolling update). Progress: node group 1 of 4 updated.

pagerduty-bot: If not resolved, escalation to platform-oncall in 6m.

maria: batch eval interim — when running v1.9 we see baseline hallucination; v2 on current kernel shows ~55% higher hallucination rate on our sample. Kernel rollback preliminary tests on a staging shard show ~60% improvement.

simon: good — keep v1.9 pinned for all critical routes until we confirm. maria, please open the incident ticket and start postmortem stub.

maria: filing incident: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-4721 (draft created, severity candidate P2). I'll attach eval set and diffs.

simon: CS/customer comms: @cs_lead can you draft a short status for any customers that asked? Keep it factual: small subset of requests saw degraded factualness; we've pinned to prior model and rolled back a runtime change.

cs_lead: copy — will prepare a brief and drop in #support-summaries in 10m.

aj: monitoring note — eval gate false positives dropping back to baseline after routing shift + kernel rollback. I'll keep an eye for 60m.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated — pager closed by simon at 2026-03-15T14:18Z. Summary: attention-normalization kernel change in runtime-build-107 correlated with factualness regression in assistant-codegen-v2; rollback to runtime-build-106 + traffic routing pin to assistant-codegen-v1.9 resolved observed output-drift. Follow-up: full postmortem due within 72h; recommend gating CI canaries with automated eval runs.

simon: thanks all. action items: (1) add automated canary eval before kernel/runtime deploys, (2) add stricter eval-gate thresholds for rollout, (3) implement model-sticky routing fallback for fast rollback. maria/les assign owners and timelines to RFCs.

maria: will own the canary eval RFC, target PR for next sprint.

les: will own runtime gating changes.

simon: closing notes — good quick response. moving incident to postmortem queue.

[end of thread]
